decisions: Plan definitions support multiple services and immutable versions.
Shared and per-service quotas are distinct; global rights use an explicit NULL target.
Calendar week/month and rolling periods are distinct; Atlantic/Canary is explicit.
Validity expiry explicitly starts at purchase or first use.
New plans are drafts; no price, payment, billing, renewal automation, client balance or booking behavior was added.
API remains local-only without runtime authentication; orchestrator LIVE remains disabled.
Juanjo approved blocking global/specific quota overlap for the same right and period; distinct service targets and distinct periods remain allowed.

open_decisions.question: Must each plan_services entry be covered by an explicit service_access right, or does inclusion itself grant service access?
open_decisions.impact: Defines future entitlement and booking authorization semantics.

non_blocking_findings: Concurrent archive race tests use Promise.all state assertions and could be made deterministic with explicit lock/wait coordination.
An INSERT into a frozen archived plan version is not separately tested, although frozen INSERT is tested after activation and the same trigger applies.
Direct SQL can change a service referenced by an active plan from active to draft; the guard currently blocks only archival.
A service can be reactivated inside an archived area, and plan_services can reference an archived service through direct SQL.
idempotency_key and request_hash remain mutable on draft and archived plan rows through direct SQL.
Several distinct 55000 failures share a generic immutable-definition HTTP message.
Concurrent quota protection relies on alphabetical PostgreSQL trigger ordering; document this dependency or combine the guards.
The database timezone catalog accepts names such as Factory although the API currently only accepts Atlantic/Canary.
An active plan cannot advance to a new current_version; the publication/versioning behavior remains a product decision.
